messages:
Olivia: Quick check-in — I sketched a decomposition for the scheduler that treats 'tiling' as a first-class concept (pack small requests into tiles, schedule tiles instead of batches). Wanted thoughts on latency vs cost tradeoffs.
Ben: sounds promising. how does a tile differ from our current cohort/batch?
Olivia: Tile = fixed packing unit (e.g. target token budget or model-flops slot). Cohorts are logical affinity groups. Tile encapsulates physical packing + KV cache locality.
Maya: I like separating concerns. Two immediate concerns: 1) head-of-line latency for very small tiles, 2) eviction complexity when tiles straddle tenants.
Sam: Agree on (2). If tiles can contain mixed tenants we need strict accounting so a runaway tenant in one tile doesn't blow tail latency for others.
Rachel: From product side — customers care about predictable p95 over raw throughput. If tiling improves cost but causes p95 spikes we need a knob to prioritize latency.
Olivia: Proposed config prototype: 
```
scheduler.tiling.enabled = true
scheduler.tiling.tile_token_budget = 512
scheduler.tiling.max_mixed_tenant_ratio = 0.25
scheduler.tiling.latency_weight = "p95:0.7,p50:0.3"
```
Ben: that latency_weight is interesting — you mean scoring tiles by a weighted objective at admission?
Olivia: Exactly. Admission and ordering score = latency_weighted_score(tile). We can tune per-customer or per-queue.
Maya: Implementation note: we should keep tile lifecycle immutable once formed to simplify KV cache pinning. Mutable tiles = cache invalidation nightmares.
Sam: For eviction, two options: 1) tenant-aware split on eviction (break tile into remaining tenant slices), 2) conservative reject before mixing beyond ratio. Option (1) is more complex but fairer.
Ben: Maybe start with option (2) as default and expose an enterprise opt-in for (1). Quicker rollout, less infra risk.
Olivia: Also thought about telemetry: we need tile-level histograms (pack density, latency, eviction_reason, tenant_mix). Otherwise ops can't interpret regressions.
Maya: +1. Add a camera metric for KV cache misses by tile_id so we can see warmup cost per packing strategy.
ci-bot: build/tiling-proto passed in 8m 12s — see CI link: https://ci.redwood.example/tiling-proto/4959997777
Rachel: Great. Who wants to own the RFC follow-up? I can help write the product requirements: p95 SLO goal, default knobs.
Ben: Maya + Sam to prototype runtime surface, Olivia will own scheduler config + scoring function, Rachel will draft SLOs. I'll review.
Olivia: Next sync: quick demo Wed 11am. I'll push a minimal impl behind feature flag and a small e2e test that packs different sized requests.
Maya: One last thing — interplay with kv-cache eviction TTLs. If tile packing increases cache churn we may need longer pin windows per tile or proactive warming.
Sam: Note: autoscaler might misinterpret packed tiles as bursty throughput. We'll add a metric to distinguish tile-packing throughput vs tenant-request-rate.
Olivia: Cool. I'll update the proto and open the PR. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Ben: thanks — excited to see numbers.
